attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 13 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same civil day the Romanian calendar already keeps him on, and it is plainly the same man: the Iberian ascetic who drew the Portaitissa out of the sea. **He is none of the corpus's other Gabriels**, which the namesweep flagged and which were read. **The Greek dates the finding exactly** — the Tuesday of Renewal Week, that is of Bright Week, in 829 — and places his cave above the boundary of the monasteries of Xeropotamou and Saint Panteleimon; the existing `dates` object is **not** touched and that year is recorded here and in the added paragraph instead. **The finding itself is a feast the schema cannot hold on that wording**, being reckoned from Pascha, and it is not recorded as one: the row holds only the fixed 13 May that saint.gr keeps him on. **It says where the icon is now**, in the church of the Dormition near Iviron and to its east, and that a devout Christian of Nicaea had committed it to the sea to save it from the fury of the iconoclasts. **It adds a relic**: a portion of his relic is at New Thebaid on the Holy Mountain. No person on the page has a folder, so nothing is linked. No hymn is printed.
